document.title: Alexander Lyakhovsky's Account of the Decision of the CC CPSU to Send Troops to Afghanistan, from The Tragedy and Valor of Afghan (Moscow, 1995)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Memoir/book excerpt giving a detailed account of how the final decision to send troops was made. The only documentary evidence of that secret decision is the handwritten Dec. 12, 1979 document.

events.description: Narrow Politburo circle meets in Brezhnev's office to discuss Afghanistan; decide to develop two options: remove Amin via KGB, or send troops.
Ustinov informs Ogarkov of preliminary decision to introduce troops (75-80 thousand); Ogarkov objects; 'small Politburo' tentatively orders preparations.
Ustinov gathers MoD Collegium; Directive #312/12/00133 sent; formation of a new Army in the Turkestan military district begins.
Ustinov summons Gen. Zaplatin to Moscow to report on the Afghan army.
Politburo unanimously decides to introduce Soviet troops into Afghanistan, termed 'the measures'; protocol handwritten by Chernenko.
Narrow Politburo meeting in Brezhnev's office discussed introducing Soviet troops into Afghanistan; decided to develop two options (remove Amin via KGB, or send troops).
Ustinov summoned Ogarkov, told him of preliminary decision, ordered preparation of 75-80 thousand troops; Ogarkov objected.
Ogarkov summoned to Brezhnev's office before the 'small Politburo'; argued for a political solution; decision deferred but troop preparations ordered.
Ustinov gathered the Ministry of Defense Collegium; Directive #312/12/00133 sent to troops; formation of new Army in Turkestan military district began.
Ustinov summoned Zaplatin to Moscow to report on the Afghan army.
Politburo elite unanimously decided to introduce Soviet troops into Afghanistan, termed 'the measures'; protocol handwritten by Chernenko.

sources_cited: Protocol of the 12 December 1979 CC CPSU Politburo session handwritten by K.U. Chernenko
Coded telegram from KGB representative B. Ivanov
Testimony of General-Major V. P. Zaplatin
key_claims: The 12 December 1979 Politburo decision to send troops into Afghanistan was taken unanimously on the initiative of Andropov, Ustinov and Gromyko.
Chief of General Staff Ogarkov opposed the intervention as 'reckless' and urged a political solution but was overruled.
Preparations (formation of a new Army in Turkestan MD) began from 10 December, before the final decision.
Soviet justifications included alleged CIA plans, possible US Pershing missiles in Afghanistan, Afghan uranium and Pakistani annexation of northern Afghanistan.
KGB assessments, notably General Ivanov's report, outweighed Gen. Zaplatin's doubts that the situation was exaggerated.
No formal Supreme Soviet decree was issued; orders were oral to ensure secrecy and mislead Amin.
Kosygin opposed the decision and did not attend the session.
